_comment: Validate-mode golden: design §9's leakage checker at its *note*
severity -- an undocumented helper that appears only in bodies the tool
never renders. Hand-written IR, like its three siblings, because the rule
is Tier A: what the front end contributes is the `body_uses` list below,
and a list is as easy to write as to compute.
Two positives, one per body, both hidden *functions* the roster says the
reader cannot see: `hard_reset` (an unmarked private member) and `clone`
(a `\merge`d twin). `hard_reset` is used by two different bodies and is
reported twice -- once per body, since the finding is about the body, not
about the declaration (the private-data nudge's rule; a Note there too).
`construct` is the control that costs the most to get wrong: it is an
`\omit`ted function used by a body *and* named in the extracted
*Equivalent to:* body below. That makes it design §9's **error** case,
which check_leakage reports -- and §9's note clause says *only* in
non-extracted bodies, so this rule must stay silent about it. One finding
for `construct` in the expectation, not two.
Three more controls that must stay silent:
- `size` is described, so a body calling it is a body calling the
class's own public interface -- the ordinary case, and the loudest
one if this rule got it wrong;
- `cache_` is hidden private *data*, which design §6's nudge
reports at its declaration instead. Reporting it here as well fired
on eleven of the seventeen corpus headers; see check_unextracted_uses
(validate.cpp) for the measurement. Nothing in this roster is marked
`\expos`, which is what keeps that §6 nudge itself silent here --
it has its own golden, and one fixture should exercise one rule;
- `tmp` is in no roster at all -- a local, a parameter or a `std::`
name as far as anything downstream can tell, and the same silence
the checker's roster half keeps for a name it does not recognize.
Exit 1 (the validate default) comes from `construct`'s leakage Error, not
from anything this rule reports: its every finding is a Note.
validate.test.cpp pins the severity directly.
